scope: Corollary F.10 (Finite residues under the actual tilted law) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 144-145. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix centers and an error η > 0. Prescribe a finite family of joint residue vectors, each consisting of polynomially many spatial residues 144 and integer coefficient lifts βh or their integer-linear coordinates z, w, modulo a common modulus M for that vector. The maximum of log M and the logarithm of the family size have prescribed bounds. Include these bounds in the Fourier budget of Lemma F.7. For every vector in the family, its joint distribution under Equation (F.4) is within η in total variation of the following comparison law: sample the coefficient-chart residues on the Haar cover with density D, and independently sample the corresponding spatial residues under the unweighted law ρ. Exact independence in this comparison law is not an assertion of exact independence under the tilted law. This permits a family of separate tests modulo prime powers at most Q and modulo prescribed bounded products of witness prime powers. It does not assert a joint approximation modulo the product of all primes at most Q, whose logarithm need not have the permitted bound. The rank threshold and parent side cutoff may depend on the maximum individual log M, the log family count, and log η−1; previously fixed bounds for the chart maps and coefficient-law parameters do not.
